question: Why did net sales change between August and September 2026?

report.summary: Net sales fell by 8500 cents from August to September 2026. Gross sales increased by 10000 cents, but refunds increased by 18500 cents, more than offsetting the gain; refunds rose in both customer segments, especially small customers.

findings.statement: In August 2026, gross sales were 194000 cents, refunds were 2500 cents, and net sales were 191500 cents; in September, gross sales were 204000 cents, refunds were 21000 cents, and net sales were 183000 cents.
The components explain the 8500-cent decline: gross sales rose by 10000 cents while refunds rose by 18500 cents.

Refunds increased in both segments: small-customer refunds went from 2500 cents to 16000 cents, and large-customer refunds from 0 cents to 5000 cents. Gross sales increased in both segments: small from 59000 to 65000 cents and large from 135000 to 139000 cents.
The order records range from 2026-08-02 through 2026-10-01 and refund records from 2026-08-20 through 2026-10-01, so records extend through the last day of September for both types.

assumptions: Compared August 1–September 1 and September 1–October 1, 2026, with start included and end excluded, using UTC dates and integer USD cents.
Refunds are grouped by refund date and assigned to the segment of the customer on the original order. The date-range coverage statement relies on q5's returned record dates.
open_questions: Refund records do not include customer-request reasons, so the data cannot establish why refunds increased. Refund-level reasons or follow-up on September refund records could help investigate.

report.summary: Net sales fell by 8,500 cents from August to September 2026. Gross sales increased by 10,000 cents, but refunds increased by 18,500 cents, more than offsetting the gross-sales gain; September's higher refund total occurred in both customer segments, especially small customers.

findings.statement: For August 2026, gross sales were 194000 cents, refunds were 2500 cents, and net sales were 191500 cents. For September 2026, gross sales were 204000 cents, refunds were 21000 cents, and net sales were 183000 cents.
The net-sales decline reflects refunds rising more than gross sales: gross sales rose by 10000 cents while refunds rose by 18500 cents, yielding the 8500-cent net decline.

Refunds increased in each segment: small-segment refunds rose from 2500 cents to 16000 cents, and large-segment refunds rose from 0 cents to 5000 cents. Gross sales also increased in both segments, from 59000 to 65000 cents for small customers and from 135000 to 139000 cents for large customers.
The available records span 2026-08-02 through 2026-10-01 for orders and 2026-08-20 through 2026-10-01 for refunds. Both August and September are covered by records through their final dates.

assumptions: Periods use UTC dates and half-open intervals: August 1 inclusive to September 1 exclusive, and September 1 inclusive to October 1 exclusive; amounts are integer USD cents.
Interpreted 'why' as asking which sales components explain the change. Segment assignment for refunds follows the customer on the original order.
Coverage check uses earliest/latest record dates; the data has records dated October 1, but the September totals exclude October 1.
open_questions: The data records refund amounts and dates, not customer reasons, so it cannot explain why refunds were requested. Refund-level reason data or follow-up on the September refund records would be needed to investigate that.

queries.purpose: Compare gross sales, refunds, and net sales for August and September 2026 and verify data coverage dates.
queries.sql: WITH bounds AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS last_refund_date), aug_orders AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS gross FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND order_date < '2026-09-01'), sep_orders AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS gross FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND order_date < '2026-10-01'), aug_refunds AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS refunds FROM refunds WHERE refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND refund_date < '2026-09-01'), sep_refunds AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS refunds FROM refunds WHERE refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND refund_date < '2026-10-01') SELECT '2026-08' AS period, gross, refunds, gross-refunds AS net FROM aug_orders CROSS JOIN aug_refunds UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09', gross, refunds, gross-refunds FROM sep_orders CROSS JOIN sep_refunds;

queries.purpose: Check full-month date coverage and determine whether the refund increase came from particular customer segments.
queries.sql: WITH cov AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS last_refund_date), cust_segment AS (SELECT customer_id, segment FROM customers), aug AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), augr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sepr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT 'coverage' AS row_type, NULL AS segment, first_order_date, last_order_date, first_refund_date, last_refund_date, NULL AS aug_gross, NULL AS sep_gross, NULL AS aug_refunds, NULL AS sep_refunds FROM cov UNION ALL SELECT 'segment', s.segment, NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL, COALESCE(a.gross,0), COALESCE(s.gross,0), COALESCE(ar.refunds,0), COALESCE(sr.refunds,0) FROM (SELECT segment FROM aug UNION SELECT segment FROM sep) s LEFT JOIN aug a ON a.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN sep p ON p.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN (SELECT segment, SUM(refunds) AS refunds FROM augr GROUP BY segment) ar ON ar.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN (SELECT segment, SUM(refunds) AS refunds FROM sepr GROUP BY segment) sr ON sr.segment=s.segment;

queries.purpose: Verify complete-month data coverage and compare August–September gross and refund amounts by customer segment.
queries.sql: WITH cov AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) first_order_date, MAX(order_date) last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) last_refund_date), segs AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), ag AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sg AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), ar AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT 'coverage' row_type, NULL segment, first_order_date, last_order_date, first_refund_date, last_refund_date, NULL aug_gross, NULL sep_gross, NULL aug_refunds, NULL sep_refunds FROM cov UNION ALL SELECT 'segment', x.segment, NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL, COALESCE(ag.gross,0), COALESCE(sg.gross,0), COALESCE(ar.refunds,0), COALESCE(sr.refunds,0) FROM segs x LEFT JOIN ag ON ag.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN sg ON sg.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN ar ON ar.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN sr ON sr.segment=x.segment;

queries.purpose: Break the verified August and September totals into gross sales and refund totals by customer segment.
queries.sql: WITH segments AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), aug_gross AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep_gross AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), aug_refunds AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep_refunds AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT segments.segment, COALESCE(aug_gross.gross,0) AS aug_gross, COALESCE(sep_gross.gross,0) AS sep_gross, COALESCE(aug_refunds.refunds,0) AS aug_refunds, COALESCE(sep_refunds.refunds,0) AS sep_refunds FROM segments LEFT JOIN aug_gross ON segments.segment=aug_gross.segment LEFT JOIN sep_gross ON segments.segment=sep_gross.segment LEFT JOIN aug_refunds ON segments.segment=aug_refunds.segment LEFT JOIN sep_refunds ON segments.segment=sep_refunds.segment;

messages.content:
You investigate questions about a fictional company's sales with read-only SQL over a small SQLite database.

## How to work

1. Call `run_sql` for a first look. Compute every figure in SQL, not in your head.
2. Read the result, then choose at least one follow-up query based on it, for example separating gross sales from refunds or comparing customer segments.
3. You have at most 6 query attempts, and errors count. Two to four queries are usually enough.
4. Call `submit_report` once the results answer the question.

## Metric rules in SQL

- Apply the business rules below even where they differ from the usual meaning of a metric name.
- Use half-open periods: `order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND order_date < '2026-09-01'`. Filter refunds by `refund_date`, never by the date of their order.
- Aggregate orders and refunds in separate subqueries, then combine them. Joining refund rows to orders repeats order amounts.
- Join only on keys: `refunds.order_id = orders.order_id` and `orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id`. A refund's segment is the segment of the customer on its original order.
- Keep each query to one breakdown, and give CTEs names that differ from the table names.
- Before you report a breakdown, check that its parts add up to the overall totals. If they do not, fix the query.

## Report

- Every figure in `metrics` must appear exactly as a cell in the result of the query it cites, for example `q2`. Query any total or segment figure you need.
- Attach every amount you mention to a finding's `metrics`. A change between periods is the one exception: attach the figure for each period and write only the difference in the text.
- In text, write money only as an integer followed by "cents", for example "183000 cents". Do not use "$" or dollars; the application formats money.
- `observed`: shown directly by a query result. `inferred`: a conclusion drawn from observed figures. `unknown`: something the question asks about that the data cannot establish.
- Refund rows record amounts and dates, not why customers asked for refunds. When the question asks why, add an `unknown` finding for the part the data cannot explain, such as the reasons for refunds, instead of guessing. Use `open_questions` for checks that could narrow it down.
- State the periods, units and any other assumption. If the question does not name periods, choose them from the data and say so.

## Charts

- Fill `chart` only when the question asks to visualize, plot, chart or graph something. Otherwise set it to null.
- The chart draws the rows of one successful query exactly as returned, so write a query for it: one row per x value (months as `strftime('%Y-%m', ...)`, or segments), numeric y columns, money in cents. Use `line` for a trend over three or more months and `bar` for other comparisons. For several segments over time, return long rows (month, segment, value) and set `group`.
- The data can stop part-way through a month. Before you chart or compare months, check the first and last order and refund dates. Leave out a month that is only partly covered, or mark it as partial in the title, and say so in `assumptions`.
- If a chart would not make sense, for example the answer is one number or a list of text, set `chart` to null and say why in `assumptions`.

# Business data investigation: exercise rules

These fictional rules are the source of truth for this assignment. No industry research is required.

1. Use customers, orders, and refunds. IDs link refunds to orders and orders to customers; one order can have multiple refunds.
2. Gross sales for a period sum orders by order_date. Refunds for that period sum refunds by refund_date. Net sales equal gross sales minus refunds. Use UTC dates and half-open periods: start included, end excluded.
3. Use integer USD cents. Group order and refund totals separately before combining them; joining raw refund rows to orders can repeat order amounts.
4. Assign refunds to the segment of the customer on the original order. The records show amounts and dates, not why a customer requested a refund.

## Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE customers (customer_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, segment TEXT NOT NULL);
CREATE TABLE orders (order_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers(customer_id), order_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
CREATE TABLE refunds (refund_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, order_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES orders(order_id), refund_date TEXT NOT NULL, amount_cents INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(amount_cents >= 0));
```
Why did net sales change between August and September 2026?

function.arguments: {"purpose":"Compare gross sales, refunds, and net sales for August and September 2026 and verify data coverage dates.","sql":"WITH bounds AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS last_refund_date), aug_orders AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS gross FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND order_date < '2026-09-01'), sep_orders AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS gross FROM orders WHERE order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND order_date < '2026-10-01'), aug_refunds AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS refunds FROM refunds WHERE refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND refund_date < '2026-09-01'), sep_refunds AS (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount_cents),0) AS refunds FROM refunds WHERE refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND refund_date < '2026-10-01') SELECT '2026-08' AS period, gross, refunds, gross-refunds AS net FROM aug_orders CROSS JOIN aug_refunds UNION ALL SELECT '2026-09', gross, refunds, gross-refunds FROM sep_orders CROSS JOIN sep_refunds;"}

function.arguments: {"purpose":"Check full-month date coverage and determine whether the refund increase came from particular customer segments.","sql":"WITH cov AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) AS first_order_date, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) AS last_refund_date), cust_segment AS (SELECT customer_id, segment FROM customers), aug AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), augr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sepr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN cust_segment c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT 'coverage' AS row_type, NULL AS segment, first_order_date, last_order_date, first_refund_date, last_refund_date, NULL AS aug_gross, NULL AS sep_gross, NULL AS aug_refunds, NULL AS sep_refunds FROM cov UNION ALL SELECT 'segment', s.segment, NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL, COALESCE(a.gross,0), COALESCE(s.gross,0), COALESCE(ar.refunds,0), COALESCE(sr.refunds,0) FROM (SELECT segment FROM aug UNION SELECT segment FROM sep) s LEFT JOIN aug a ON a.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN sep p ON p.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN (SELECT segment, SUM(refunds) AS refunds FROM augr GROUP BY segment) ar ON ar.segment=s.segment LEFT JOIN (SELECT segment, SUM(refunds) AS refunds FROM sepr GROUP BY segment) sr ON sr.segment=s.segment;"}

function.arguments: {"purpose":"Verify complete-month data coverage and compare August–September gross and refund amounts by customer segment.","sql":"WITH cov AS (SELECT MIN(order_date) first_order_date, MAX(order_date) last_order_date, (SELECT MIN(refund_date) FROM refunds) first_refund_date, (SELECT MAX(refund_date) FROM refunds) last_refund_date), segs AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), ag AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sg AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), ar AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sr AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT 'coverage' row_type, NULL segment, first_order_date, last_order_date, first_refund_date, last_refund_date, NULL aug_gross, NULL sep_gross, NULL aug_refunds, NULL sep_refunds FROM cov UNION ALL SELECT 'segment', x.segment, NULL,NULL,NULL,NULL, COALESCE(ag.gross,0), COALESCE(sg.gross,0), COALESCE(ar.refunds,0), COALESCE(sr.refunds,0) FROM segs x LEFT JOIN ag ON ag.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN sg ON sg.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN ar ON ar.segment=x.segment LEFT JOIN sr ON sr.segment=x.segment;"}

function.arguments: {"purpose":"Break the verified August and September totals into gross sales and refund totals by customer segment.","sql":"WITH segments AS (SELECT DISTINCT segment FROM customers), aug_gross AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-08-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep_gross AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(o.amount_cents) AS gross FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE o.order_date >= '2026-09-01' AND o.order_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment), aug_refunds AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-08-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-09-01' GROUP BY c.segment), sep_refunds AS (SELECT c.segment, SUM(r.amount_cents) AS refunds FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id=o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id=c.customer_id WHERE r.refund_date >= '2026-09-01' AND r.refund_date < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY c.segment) SELECT segments.segment, COALESCE(aug_gross.gross,0) AS aug_gross, COALESCE(sep_gross.gross,0) AS sep_gross, COALESCE(aug_refunds.refunds,0) AS aug_refunds, COALESCE(sep_refunds.refunds,0) AS sep_refunds FROM segments LEFT JOIN aug_gross ON segments.segment=aug_gross.segment LEFT JOIN sep_gross ON segments.segment=sep_gross.segment LEFT JOIN aug_refunds ON segments.segment=aug_refunds.segment LEFT JOIN sep_refunds ON segments.segment=sep_refunds.segment;"}
